title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that compares a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline to accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and a deterministic validator, we selected K=200 tasks deterministically and evaluated a single shared generator output per task. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair step was never invoked. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. All execution and scoring artifacts are archived for deterministic replay (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6). The exact initial master prompt used to initiate autonomous execution is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). We interpret this as a ceiling/null result specific to the tested regime and give artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Automated intent→configuration translation promises large operational savings but risks introducing changes that break reachability, service SLAs, or dependents. The generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) architecture—where an LLM proposes a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks safety/policy, and an automated repair step attempts fixes before apply—has been proposed to bound those risks. However, there is little preregistered, artifact‑archived causal evidence estimating the verifier/repair marginal effect under reproducible sampling rules. We therefore preregistered (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) and executed a paired experiment that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect while holding generator output fixed per task. Research question: To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared to accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and at what controller/model cost? Principal contribution: (1) a fully preregistered, deterministic, paired evaluation (K=200 tasks) with complete artifact hashing and provenance; (2) a deterministic, reproducible ceiling/null result (no discordant pairs; repairs unused) together with archived traces for deterministic replay; and (3) a concrete, artifact‑grounded discussion of experimental contracts effective for measuring verifier value in future work.
sections.related_work: Prior work frames GenAI for NetOps around generate→validate→repair and tool‑augmented agentic workflows that rely on deterministic verifiers or formal solvers to limit operational risk. Benchmarks and prototypes (Cornetto et al.; TypoNet; work on generate–validate–repair paradigms) motivate confirmatory designs that measure how much verification reduces harmful proposals at scale. Our study differs by (i) preregistering a paired estimator with deterministic selection rules and (ii) publishing a complete artifact manifest (model calls, validator traces, selection manifests, and analysis code) to enable bit‑exact replay.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The experiment preregistration (cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) fixed all design choices before observing results: K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a public intent pool by SHA‑256(intent) ascending sort; paired design with two conditions per task (baseline: accept LLM suggestion; guarded: run verifier and allow one repair attempt if verifier fails); a single shared_initial_generation per task (both arms used the same generator candidate) so the paired contrast isolates the verifier+repair marginality; maximum_model_calls = 400 (predeclared), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate with one initial generation call per task, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Model and agentic setup. Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa); adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task selection, inclusion/exclusion. Tasks were filtered to intents that the preregistered validator reported as covered (inclusion automated). The deterministic selection produced 200 unique tasks; all excluded/omitted items would have been logged in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). Execution and artifact capture. The run archived every model prompt/response, provider call trace, verifier trace, and per‑episode scoring JSON. Key artifact fingerprints: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = 79c91155...), and the full execution manifest with per‑file SHA‑256s (see artifact table). Analysis plan. Primary confirmatory test: paired binary difference (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) tested with exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) to obtain a 95% percentile CI. The analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and seeds are archived; analytic outputs and contingency tables are in analysis/*.csv.
sections.results: Execution and outcomes. Planned episodes: 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (one shared generator call per task); the repair pathway was not exercised: repair_applied=false in every scoring JSON. Primary paired contingency: n11=200 (both arms success), n10=0 (guarded success only), n01=0 (baseline success only), n00=0 (both fail). Observed rates: baseline = 200/200 (100% validator‑compliant applies); guarded = 200/200 (100%). Inferential result: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. Representative per‑task diagnostics. Every execution/scoring JSON contains deterministic validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot). Example archived episode traces: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 3055f874...) and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = d10b415a...). Repair usage and cost accounting. The verifier never returned a failing verdict for any shared_initial_candidate in the selected sample; thus no repair calls were made and model_call budget used equals the number of tasks (200). The archived provider_call traces and response files permit exact accounting of tokens/calls for alternate replay. Aggregated difficulty/coverage summary request (peer review). The per‑task difficulty label and validator coverage indicator are present in each archived scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json) and in the task_manifest entries; however, the autonomous analysis pipeline did not produce an aggregated difficulty table during the run. We therefore do not invent aggregated counts here. Auditors or readers can reproduce the requested aggregation deterministically by parsing execution/scoring/*.json (or execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and counting the difficulty labels (fields such as difficulty.level) and validator coverage flags; representative files and exact paths are listed in the artifact table (execution/scoring/*.json; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). For deterministic replay we supply the relevant artifact fingerprints (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R yields fewer regression‑causing applies than accepting the LLM suggestion directly) was not supported in this sampling/model/validator regime: both arms produced validator‑compliant applies for every selected task and repairs were never invoked. This outcome is a reproducible ceiling/null result under the stated experimental contract—not evidence that verifiers are universally unnecessary. Key design observations and implications: (1) Sampling dependence: by construction tasks were filtered to intents the deterministic validator declared as covered; this inclusion rule intentionally reduced verifier‑exercising failure prevalence and therefore produced a low‑variance, ceiling sample. Measuring verifier marginal value therefore requires sampling that intentionally includes failure‑rich or adversarial intents, or sampling from historical production incidents. (2) Shared_initial_generation vs closed‑loop estimands: fixing the generator output per task isolates verifier+repair marginality but prevents generator adaptation to verifier feedback; evaluating end‑to‑end benefit of a G→V→R pipeline in practice likely requires closed‑loop estimands where the generator can regenerate candidates after validator failures. (3) Model/validator pairing: results are specific to the requested model (gpt-5-mini) and to the deterministic validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Replaying the run with weaker generators, alternative validator coverage, or adversarial prompts will alter outcomes; all artifacts needed for deterministic replay are archived. Reproducibility and audit. We provide precise, immutable hashes for core artifacts to enable bit‑exact replay: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...), and provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). Threats to validity. Internal validity: fixed shared initial generation reduces generator variability but forfeits closed‑loop effects; no technical restarts affected scientific outcomes. Construct validity: our binary validator outcome (validator.valid) depends on the fidelity of deterministic_netops_validator_v5; blind spots in the validator would understate real regressions. External validity: single model, synthetic deterministic selection, and inclusion restricted to validator‑covered intents limit generalization to production distributions. Conclusion validity: degenerate counts (all successes) produce a null difference; bootstrap CI and McNemar p correctly reflect the observed sample but do not imply a universal absence of verifier value.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministic, paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected by SHA‑256 sort from validator‑covered intents; shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), both baseline and guarded arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported for this tested regime (paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). The repair pathway was never exercised. This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...; model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...; master prompt provenance SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). We recommend that future confirmatory work (i) deliberately sample failure‑rich or adversarial intents, (ii) consider closed‑loop generator–validator estimands that allow regeneration on validator failure, and (iii) report aggregated per‑task difficulty and validator coverage statistics (those per‑task fields are present in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl and allow deterministic aggregation). All artifacts required to reproduce, aggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed for audit and independent analysis.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for true operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
